key_decisions.decision: Keeps the allegation in the officials’ speech, all eight peoples, and the link to practices without adding a racial doctrine.
Retains the consequential holy seed expression and leadership responsibility; explains the image without endorsing later racial uses.
Preserves Ezra’s bodily distress and the two garments without softening self-inflicted pain.
Preserves the short respite, tent peg, brightened eyes, and limited life amid continuing slavery.
Retains repeated slavery and the protective-wall image without asserting a completed city wall.
Preserves the quoted prophetic summary as Ezra presents it, without identifying it as one verbatim Torah passage.
Keeps both marriage directions, the severe prohibition, and the stated inheritance purpose without softening their scope.
Keeps the final tension of standing before God while unable to stand, without supplying a reassuring resolution.
